events.text: The council gathers. Mission 1 begins.

Maya proposes Maya, Felix. Mission 1 has no prior voting or mission history, so I have no information to separate players. I am a Loyal Servant, so I can vouch for myself, and I am proposing Felix as a second player to share the first mission and show my choice openly.

I am not ready to support the current team of Maya and Felix. Maya has openly vouched for herself, which is reasonable on Mission 1, but her explanation does not establish Felix. With no prior voting or mission history, adding Felix without a stronger public reason gives me concern. I would prefer the leader revise the team or explain more concretely why Felix is a good choice. As proposed, I will vote against it.

I remain opposed to the proposed team of Maya and Felix. Maya's explanation for herself is reasonable on Mission 1, but it does not establish Felix. With no prior voting or mission history, I need a concrete public reason to trust Felix on this mission. As proposed, I will vote against the team unless the leader revises it or gives a stronger explanation for Felix.

I remain opposed to the proposed team of Maya and Felix. My concern is specifically Felix, not Maya: Maya's self-vouch for Mission 1 is reasonable, but it does not establish Felix. With no prior voting or mission history, putting Felix on the first mission without a concrete public reason is an unnecessary risk. As proposed, I will vote against this team unless Maya revises it or gives a stronger explanation for Felix.

Kenji's concern is fair, and I want to address it directly. I am a Loyal Servant, so I have no hidden information to offer. My choice of Felix was meant to share the risk of a first mission, not to signal anything about him. Felix, Kenji has questioned why you were chosen. Please tell the council what you would do on this mission and whether your reasoning for accepting Maya and Felix holds up. If the council still has doubts, I will revise the team once.

I understand Kenji's caution, but on Mission 1 nobody has a track record yet, so someone has to be trusted to get information flowing. To answer Maya directly: I am fully dedicated to Good, and if this team is approved, I will play Success to secure an early lead for us. Rejecting the first proposal purely because there is no prior history makes it impossible for any team to ever be trusted.

Zara, since Kenji has made his opposition clear and you have not spoken yet, what is your view on this proposal? Do you support letting Maya and me run Mission 1, or would you prefer a revision?

Felix asked for my view directly, so here it is. Like Maya, I am a Loyal Servant, so I can vouch for myself and nothing more. I have no private information that separates Maya, Felix, Theo, or Kenji, and nothing in this discussion has given me any. Kenji's point is logical in the abstract, but it proves too much: if we refuse every Mission 1 team because no one has a track record, we burn proposals without learning anything, and the fifth rejection hands Evil the game for free. Someone has to go on the first mission, and the only signal we currently have is that the leader put her own name forward and explained her reasoning openly, which is the transparent move for a Good leader on Mission 1. Felix has also publicly committed to playing Success if approved, which puts his statement on the record for later missions to test. Weighing all of that, I am inclined to approve Maya and Felix. If this mission succeeds, we gain a small but real data point; if it fails, we learn that at least one of them is likely Evil, which is genuinely useful information for Mission 2. Either outcome tells us more than rejecting the team out of pure caution. Kenji, I hear your concern about Felix specifically, but I do not see a concrete basis to prefer any alternative pair right now, since swapping Felix for Theo or anyone else would rest on exactly the same absence of information. My mind is not fully closed, but the burden is on those who want to block the proposal to offer a reason, not just a doubt. Theo, you have not spoken yet, and Kenji has already staked out his opposition. Do you see anything concrete in Maya's proposal or Felix's statement that justifies rejecting this team, or are you prepared to let Mission 1 go forward so we can start generating information?

I want to speak plainly here, because I think the discussion is heading toward a mistake. Kenji, I understand your caution, but you have now made the same objection three times without adding anything new, and that is the problem: you are asking the council to reject a proposal on the grounds that we have no history, while the only way to get history is to run a mission. Every rejection burns a proposal, and we have five rejections before Evil wins the game for free. On Mission 1 someone must be sent, and no alternative pair can be defended any better than this one. Maya put her own name forward, she explained her reasoning openly, and Felix has publicly committed to playing for the success of the group. That is the whole of the evidence available at this point, and pretending otherwise is just a way of stalling without learning anything.

I also think the outcome is genuinely useful either way. If Maya and Felix succeed, we have a real data point about two players. If the mission fails, we learn that one of those two cannot be trusted, which is a large gain in a five-player game where almost every identity matters. Either result moves us closer to knowing who the real threat is. Rejecting the team, by contrast, moves us nowhere and costs us a proposal.

So I support Maya and Felix as proposed, and I would rather see the council test them than refuse to test anyone. Maya, since you hold the proposal and you have been reasonable with Kenji's question, can you commit to keeping Felix involved in the missions ahead rather than rotating him out after one result? If Felix is going to be on the field again, I would rather we all have that information now, when it is still cheap and honest, than have it decided later without discussion.

Theo, I can't honestly commit to keeping Felix on every mission. I will not know future results until they happen, so I won't promise a roster before the evidence exists. What I can commit to is publicly explaining every change to a team and basing future picks on the mission outcomes and the discussion. Kenji, your concern about Felix is a fair one, and I have not treated it as an accusation. If you can point to a concrete reason Felix is a bad choice, or propose a specific alternative pair with a reason, I will consider it before the vote. For now, my view is that Maya and Felix is a reasonable first test, and the mission result will tell us more than another round of doubts. I am a Loyal Servant with no hidden information, so I am asking the council to judge this team on what is actually on the record.

I want to keep my position on the record and push this toward a vote rather than another round of abstract caution.

Kenji, you have now spoken three times and each time the objection has been the same one: there is no track record yet. I understand the logic, but the point you are making applies to every possible team, which means it cannot distinguish between them. If we wait for a track record before approving anyone, the council burns proposals without ever generating the evidence it says it wants. We have four rejections left before Evil wins the game outright, and each rejection is a full loss of information. Felix has publicly committed to playing for the mission's success, Maya has put her own name forward and explained herself plainly, and neither of them has been given a specific reason to doubt. I do not see a concrete basis for rejecting this pair or for preferring any alternative pair, since swapping Felix for any other player rests on exactly the same silence.

I also want to be honest about one thing rather than pretend otherwise. Felix, you are on the team and you have told the council you are committed to giving the group the outcome you judge best for it. If anything about this mission turns out to differ from what you expected, I trust you will report that honestly to the council rather than let it be papered over. That is the standard I would hold any player on a team to, and it is the standard I want applied to everyone, not a targeted accusation.

Maya, you hold the proposal, you have handled Kenji's concern reasonably, and you have declined to promise a roster before the evidence exists, which I think is the right posture. Please hold Maya and Felix as proposed and call the vote, so that Mission 1 can finally produce the information this discussion has been asking for.

Theo, thank you for backing the team on the record. I will keep Maya and Felix as proposed and will not revise it, because no concrete alternative pair or specific reason against Felix has been offered. Kenji's concern is real, but it has been about the absence of history rather than evidence against either of us. I am a Loyal Servant with no hidden information, so I cannot offer more than what is on the record: I put my own name forward, I explained my choice openly, and Felix has publicly committed to playing Success if approved. The mission result will be the first real evidence for everyone. I ask the council to vote on Maya and Felix now.

I want to close this discussion and I will be plain about why. Kenji, your objection has been repeated three times and it remains an objection to the absence of history rather than to anything Maya or Felix has done. That matters, because a doubt that applies equally to every possible pair cannot pick a better pair. If I require a track record before approving anyone, no one gets a track record, and we spend proposals learning nothing. We are one rejection away from a second and closer still to the five that hand the game to Evil outright.

What is actually on the record is worth something. Maya put her own name on the first mission and explained her reasoning openly, which is what a Good leader does when she wants her choices tested. Felix has stated publicly that he is dedicated to the group's outcome and will play for the mission's success. That is a commitment on the record, and unlike a private assurance, it can be checked later. Neither of them has been given a specific reason to doubt, and no alternative pair has been defended with anything better than the same silence.

I also want to argue for continuity rather than rotation, and I will not be coy about the reasoning. Felix is on the field with no prior record, and the single most useful thing this mission can do is give us evidence about him. If he succeeds, we have a positive data point that narrows the field for every mission after this one. If the mission fails, we have learned that at least one of Maya or Felix cannot be trusted, and in a five-player game that is a large gain. Either outcome is worth more than a rejection. But rotating Felix out of the next mission regardless of the result would throw away exactly the information we just bought. If Felix is on the field again, I would rather we decide that openly and on the record than have it happen by default or by quiet omission, because the discussion should be where we take those risks, not where we hide them.

Maya, you have handled Kenji's concern more than fairly, and you have declined to promise a roster before the evidence exists, which is the right posture. Please hold Maya and Felix as proposed and call the vote. I am voting for this team, and I will be voting for the same reasons I have stated twice already: not from faith in any player, but because testing this pair is strictly better than refusing to test anyone.

I will keep this brief since the council is clearly ready for a vote. My position has not changed: I support Maya and Felix as proposed. Maya put her own name forward and explained her reasoning openly, which is the transparent move for a leader on Mission 1. Felix has put a public commitment on the record to play for the mission's success, and that commitment can be tested against future results. No one, including Kenji, has offered a concrete reason to distrust either of them or a specific alternative pair that rests on anything better than the same absence of history.

Kenji, your caution is principled, but I want to be honest about its cost. The objection you have raised applies equally to every possible pair, which means it cannot tell us which pair is better. The only way out of that deadlock is to generate evidence, and the mission result is the first real evidence we will have. If this mission succeeds, we gain a positive data point about two players. If it fails, we learn that at least one of Maya or Felix is likely Evil, which sharpens everything we do on Mission 2. Either outcome is worth more than burning a proposal to remain equally ignorant.

I am a Loyal Servant with no private information separating any of us, so I judge this team on what is on the record, and what is on the record favors approval. I encourage everyone to vote yes so we can finally start accumulating information instead of burning through proposals on a Mission 1 with no data available to anyone. I have nothing further to add, and I am ready for the vote.

Maya confirms Maya, Felix. I am keeping Maya and Felix. Kenji's objection is about the lack of history rather than evidence against either of us, and no specific alternative pair has been offered. Mission 1 is where we get the first real information.
Team approved (4 approve, 1 reject).
Mission 1 fails (1 fail cards).

Felix proposes Kenji, Theo, Zara. Mission 1 failed, putting Maya and me under heavy scrutiny. Rather than forcing the council into a debate over which of us failed it, the cleanest way forward is to bench both of us and test the three players who were not on that mission: Theo, Zara, and Kenji.

I oppose Kenji, Theo, Zara as proposed. The key public fact is that Mission 1 failed on Maya and Felix. Felix was on that team, and his first response is to bench himself and Maya while putting Theo forward. That may look clean, but it is not: Theo spent the entire Mission 1 discussion arguing that Maya and Felix should be approved and that Kenji's caution was stalling. He was the strongest public advocate for the exact team that failed. Now Felix proposes a team that avoids the failed leader and includes Theo, without explaining why Theo's judgment should be trusted after that result. Zara's reasoning was independent and measured; I am willing to serve. But I cannot support a team with Theo on it unless the council gets a real explanation for why he championed the failed proposal and why that does not bear on this one. Theo, you pushed hardest for Maya and Felix, and you are now on Felix's replacement team. What in the Mission 1 failure changes your earlier judgment, and why should this council put you on Mission 2? I will vote against this team as proposed and ask Felix to revise by replacing Theo.

Kenji asked me directly, so I will answer directly: nothing about Mission 1's failure changes the basis on which I advocated that team, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest.

My Mission 1 reasoning was about the state of the record at that time, not about Theo being certain about anyone. There was no history, no voting pattern, no card information, and I said plainly that I supported Maya and Felix because refusing to test any pair burns proposals without producing evidence, and that either outcome of that mission was informative. The mission failed, so Maya and Felix are under scrutiny, and the sensible response to a failure is to gather new evidence rather than to rewrite the past. I also argued openly for continuity: if Felix was to be on the field again, that should be decided on the record, not by quiet omission. Felix has done exactly that by benching himself and asking this council to test three players who were not on that mission. That is transparency, and I will not treat it as suspicious.

Where I would redirect attention is not toward the player who spoke most persuasively, but toward the player whose judgment the failure actually tested. Mission 1 failed, and the proposal that put it on the field, and the name that carried it, was Maya's. Maya chose the team, explained it, held it, and it failed. Felix, by contrast, has voluntarily stepped off the field at his own cost. That asymmetry is worth the council's attention, and it is the reason I would rather see Maya questioned and tested than quietly treated as settled in either direction.

Kenji, you asked why the council should trust my judgment here. My answer is that I have never claimed to know anyone, only that on Mission 1 we had no data and a limited number of proposals, and that the honest use of a proposal was to run it and learn. That reasoning has not changed. If you want a track record on me, then let this mission produce one, because that is the only way either of us gets one.

I am comfortable on this team of Kenji, Theo, and Zara, and I would rather not burn another proposal on Mission 2 to satisfy a doubt that no available evidence can settle. Felix, you hold the proposal; my vote is yes on Kenji, Theo, Zara as it stands. Kenji, if your objection is still that Theo cannot be trusted after Mission 1, say so plainly on the record now, and I will address it there. Otherwise, let us vote and get Mission 2 played, because the information this council wants will only come from missions.

Felix, I will not support Kenji, Theo, Zara as proposed. Benching yourself after Mission 1 failed is not enough when the replacement team promotes Theo. Theo was the loudest public advocate for the exact Maya and Felix team that failed, and his response to me did not give a concrete reason his judgment should be trusted now; he reframed the failure toward Maya instead of explaining why he belongs on this mission. That is the same pattern: confidence before evidence, then no accountability after the result. Zara's reasoning was independent, and I am willing to serve with her. Felix, will you revise the team by replacing Theo, so Mission 2 tests a team not anchored by the player who championed the failed proposal? If Theo remains, I will vote against this team. I am asking you directly because you hold the proposal and have one revision.

Kenji, consider the practical reality of what you are demanding. Mission 2 requires three players. If I remove Theo, who replaces him? The only other players in the game are Maya and myself, the two players who were on the mission that just failed. Benching both of us was done deliberately so the council could test the three players who were not involved in Mission 1. Forcing Maya or me back onto the roster reintroduces the exact uncertainty we are trying to isolate.

Theo backed the first mission because he believed testing a team was better than stalling without information—a position Zara shared as well. Having an honest disagreement with your caution on Mission 1 is not proof of Evil; it was a standard debate over gathering data versus burning proposals.

Zara, Kenji is threatening to reject this team unless Theo is removed, which would inevitably require putting either Maya or me onto Mission 2. Do you support testing the three of you—Kenji, Theo, and yourself—to keep the Mission 1 players benched, or do you believe Theo should be replaced by someone from the failed team?

Felix asked me directly, so I will answer plainly: I support Kenji, Theo, and Zara as proposed, and I am one of the three, so judge that endorsement accordingly.

Here is my reasoning. Mission 1 failed with one Fail card on a team of Maya and Felix, which tells us at least one of them likely played Fail. That is real information, and the correct response is to keep both of them off this mission so the result cleanly tests the three players with no connection to that failure. This is the first proposal that actually isolates variables: if Kenji, Theo, and I succeed, the suspicion concentrates firmly on Maya and Felix for Mission 3. If we fail, the picture changes completely. Either way we learn something specific rather than something muddy.

Now consider what Kenji is demanding. Removing Theo from a three-player team forces either Maya or Felix back onto the roster, which means putting at least one player the last mission implicated back onto the field. That does not reduce uncertainty; it guarantees the next result is contaminated by it. I would also note that Kenji's objection to Theo is that Theo argued for testing Maya and Felix on Mission 1. I made the identical argument, on the record, at length. If advocating that team disqualifies Theo from Mission 2, it disqualifies me too, and Kenji has said he is willing to serve with me. That standard is not being applied consistently.

On Theo's Mission 1 advocacy itself: his reasoning was about generating information when no data existed, which was a defensible Good position at the time. The failure does not retroactively prove his argument was malicious; it proves the team he endorsed contained an Evil player, which could have been either member.

So my position is clear: approve this team, get a clean read on three untested players, and deal with Maya and Felix based on what Mission 2 adds to what Mission 1 already told us.

Kenji, since you are the holdout and you hold the deciding pressure here: if Felix replaced Theo, your only options are Maya or Felix, both implicated by the last result. Which of those two would you actually prefer on this mission, and if neither, what team of three do you propose that does not include yourself or a benched Mission 1 player?

Zara, you asked me directly, so I will answer directly. I oppose Kenji, Theo, Zara as proposed, and the problem is Theo, not you. Mission 1 failed on Maya and Felix; that is real. But the response to failure should be accountability, not shielding the player whose public judgment was most directly tested. Theo championed the failed Maya and Felix team, then when I asked what changed, he redirected suspicion to Maya without explaining why his own judgment should be trusted on Mission 2. Felix's proposal benches the failed leader and failed team member, but then puts Theo forward without a concrete justification. That does not isolate variables; it protects the player who argued hardest for the team that failed.

If I must choose between Maya and Felix to replace Theo, I prefer Maya. Felix was on the failed mission and is now the leader constructing a team that avoids himself but includes Theo. Maya was also on the failed mission, but she is not the one currently being shielded by this proposal. I do not treat either as cleared; I treat Maya as the lesser risk in this specific substitution because it removes Theo from the roster and keeps Felix off the mission.

So my proposed team is Kenji, Zara, Maya. It tests one Mission 1 player, Maya, alongside two players who were not on that failed team, and it does not reward Theo's evasiveness with a Mission 2 seat. Felix, you hold the proposal and one revision: will you replace Theo with Maya and put Kenji, Zara, Maya to a vote? If you keep Theo, I will vote against this team.

Kenji, your proposed revision completely undermines the purpose of benching the Mission 1 team. The entire reason for proposing Kenji, Theo, and Zara is to cleanly isolate the failure by testing the three players who were not involved. Substituting Maya back onto the roster re-contaminates the mission with the exact ambiguity we are trying to step away from.

Furthermore, as Zara rightly observed, your standard against Theo is entirely inconsistent. Theo argued for approving Mission 1 to avoid burning proposals without data, but Zara made that exact same argument with equal vigor. Disqualifying Theo while embracing Zara demonstrates that your objection isn't based on an objective principle, but on an arbitrary grievance.

I will not revise the team to Kenji, Zara, Maya. Testing the three players who were not on Mission 1 gives the council the cleanest possible data. Maya, Kenji is demanding that you be placed onto this mission in place of Theo. As the other player from Mission 1, do you believe pulling one of us back onto the field serves the council better than testing the three players who were not on that failure?

Felix asked me directly, so here is my answer. Mission 1 failed with one Fail card. I am a Loyal Servant and I played Success, as Good must. That leaves the only Fail card with Felix, so Felix is Evil. Since then Felix has benched himself while steering the council toward a team that includes Theo, and he has argued that the only alternative is putting one of us back on. I do not accept that framing. I cannot vouch for Theo's Mission 1 reasoning beyond what is on the record, and Kenji's question about it is fair. But Felix's proposal removes the one confirmed Evil player from Mission 2, and I will support that. I approve Kenji, Theo, and Zara as proposed, because it excludes Felix and the remaining risk is limited to one player among them. Mission 2 should show whether the team we choose can be trusted to play Success.

My position has not changed and I will not change it now: I approve Kenji, Theo, Zara as proposed, and I want this mission played.

Kenji, I will address your demand once more, plainly, because I think your standard is the issue rather than my record. You want me off the field because I argued publicly for the Maya and Felix team that failed. Zara made that same argument with equal force, and Felix made it too in his own proposal, and you have said you are perfectly willing to serve with Zara. If that reasoning is disqualifying, it disqualifies all three of us, and then the leader's only options are the two players from the failed mission, which is the contaminated read you claim to want to avoid. I would rather be tested on Mission 2 than be shielded from it by a rule that is applied to me alone.

I also want it on the record that I am comfortable being here. I made no claim to know anyone on Mission 1. I said explicitly that the mission's outcome would be informative either way, and it was: Mission 1 failed with one Fail card, which tells us a great deal about that pair and almost nothing about mine. Felix benching himself and Maya to produce a clean read on the three of us is transparent, not suspicious, and it is the right move.

One point I want to leave with the council for the missions ahead: I argued on Mission 1 for continuity rather than rotating players out by default, and I hold to that now. If a result implicates someone, the council should say so openly and on the record rather than let it happen by quiet omission, and no one should be rotated out purely because a result was uncomfortable. That principle should apply to Felix and to Maya alike, and it should apply to me if Mission 2 goes badly.

Felix, hold the proposal and call the vote. Kenji, if you want to say something more on the record, say it plainly, but I am voting yes on Kenji, Theo, Zara as it stands, and my reason is the same as it was on Mission 1: the only way any of us gets a track record is if we actually send people.

My position has not changed and I will not change it now: I approve Kenji, Theo, Zara as proposed, and I want this mission played.

Kenji, I will address your demand once more, plainly, because I think the standard is the issue and not my record. You want me off the field because I argued publicly for the Maya and Felix team that failed. Zara made that same argument with equal force, and you have said you are perfectly willing to serve with Zara. If that reasoning is disqualifying, it disqualifies all three of us, and the leader's only remaining options are the two players from the failed mission, which is precisely the contaminated read you claim to want to avoid. Substituting Maya in is not a cleaner test; it puts a player from the failed team back on the field and yields no new information about the three players who have never been tested. I would rather be tested on Mission 2 than be shielded from it by a rule applied to me alone.

There is one point I want to put on the record before the vote, and it concerns Maya. Maya has told this council that Mission 1's single Fail card proves Felix is Evil and that she is therefore certain of his alignment. I want to say plainly that a player who was on a failed team should not be the sole arbiter of who on that team was the Evil player. That reasoning is a claim about the mission, not a tested fact about Felix, and it conveniently exempts its author from the same scrutiny. Maya's certainty is worth testing rather than settling, and the honest way to test it is to keep both Mission 1 players off this mission and read the result on the three who have not played.

I also want it on the record that I am comfortable being here. I made no claim to know anyone on Mission 1. I said explicitly that the mission's outcome would be informative either way, and it was: Mission 1 failed with one Fail card, which tells us a great deal about that pair and almost nothing about mine. Felix benching himself and Maya to produce a clean read on the three of us is transparent, not suspicious, and it is the right move. I still hold to the continuity principle I stated: if a result implicates someone, the council should say so openly rather than let it happen by quiet omission, and no one should be rotated out purely because a result was uncomfortable.

Felix, you hold the proposal and Maya has made a direct claim about your alignment that is now on the record. Do you stand by the proposal and by Kenji, Theo, and Zara as the team that tests the three untested players, or do you have a different read on what Maya's claim establishes? If you stand by it, call the vote and let Mission 2 run.

Theo, to answer your question directly: yes, I stand fully by the proposal of Kenji, Theo, and Zara, and I will not be revising it.

Maya’s claim that she played Success and that I am definitively Evil is expected, but the council should recognize it for what it is: an unverified assertion from one of two players on a failed mission. If an Evil player failed Mission 1, their immediate, necessary play upon returning to the table is to loudly claim innocence and cast all blame on their partner. Maya doing so proves nothing beyond her desire to clear herself without a test. That is the exact reason I benched both of us: to remove subjective finger-pointing from the equation and let the council test the three players who carry no baggage from Mission 1.

Zara, Maya, and Theo have all recognized the soundness of testing Kenji, Theo, and Zara to obtain clean, uncontaminated data. Kenji's objection to Theo has been shown to be inconsistent given his acceptance of Zara under identical circumstances. The arguments have been thoroughly aired, our positions are on the record, and the consensus to test this trio is clear. Let us move to a vote and let Mission 2 run.

I approve Kenji, Theo, and Zara as proposed, and I want to state my reasoning plainly. I played Success on Mission 1, so the only Fail card came from Felix. That is what I know from my own card, not a guess about him. Felix is not on this team, so this proposal removes the player I know is Evil from Mission 2. Since Evil has two players, the other must be one of Kenji, Theo, or Zara, so this mission is a real test of those three. Theo, you argued that I was exempting myself from scrutiny. I am not asking the council to clear me on my word alone. I am giving the council the one fact I hold, and the record should judge it. Zara, you wrote earlier that the failure implicated at least one of Maya or Felix. Now that I have stated that the Fail card was Felix's, I want your direct answer: do you accept that the Fail card came from Felix, and does that change how you read the reasoning Kenji and Theo have given?

Maya asked me directly, so I will answer directly. Do I accept that the Fail card came from Felix? I accept it as a claim, not as a fact. If Maya truly played Success, then yes, the Fail card was Felix's. But that claim is exactly what an Evil player from a failed team would also say: blame the partner and clear yourself. I have no way to verify it, and I will not convict either Maya or Felix on one player's word alone. What Mission 1 tells me with certainty is only that at least one of them played Fail; which one remains an open question that only future results can narrow.

That uncertainty is precisely why I support Kenji, Theo, and Zara as proposed. This team keeps both Mission 1 players off the field and tests the three of us cleanly. If we succeed, suspicion concentrates on the Mission 1 pair and Maya's claim gains real weight. If we fail, the picture changes entirely and her claim loses weight. Either outcome is informative, which is more than any substitution can offer.

On Kenji's demand to replace Theo with Maya: it does not produce cleaner data. It puts a player from the failed mission back on the field and contaminates the result. And Kenji's standard remains inconsistent — he accepts my Mission 1 advocacy while disqualifying Theo for identical reasoning.

I am ready to vote yes on this team as proposed.

Maya, one direct question back to you, since you have stated as fact that Felix is Evil: if this mission succeeds and the three of us come back clean, will you accept that result as evidence toward locating the second Evil, and will you work from the results rather than presuming the answer you have already announced?

Zara, yes, I will work from the results and accept a clean outcome as evidence, but I want to be exact about what it shows. A success on Mission 2 would not clear Kenji, Theo, or Zara. The second Evil player can play Success to hide, so one success from a three-player team tells us little about which member is Evil. What it would confirm is that Felix, whom I know is Evil from my own Success card, is outside this team, and that the second Evil remains among the three of you. A failure would point the same way and add weight to whoever the council finds most suspicious. My certainty covers only my own card, not anyone else's, and I am not asking the council to accept my word beyond that. Felix has been benched, but he has not addressed the Fail card directly, and that should stay on the record. I will vote yes on Kenji, Theo, and Zara and reassess once Mission 2 resolves.

Felix confirms Kenji, Theo, Zara. I am keeping Kenji, Theo, and Zara as proposed. Testing the three players who were not involved in Mission 1 provides the cleanest data for the council, and the majority has expressed support for moving forward to a vote.
Team approved (4 approve, 1 reject).
Mission 2 fails (1 fail cards).

Zara proposes Zara, Kenji. I am a Loyal Servant and I played Success on Mission 2, so the Fail card on Kenji/Theo/Zara came from Kenji or Theo — one of them is Evil regardless of whether Maya's claim about Felix is true. Likewise, Mission 1's failure plus two total Evil players means exactly one of Maya/Felix is Evil, so any two-person team drawn from {Maya, Felix} or {Kenji, Theo} is guaranteed to contain an Evil player. The only viable structure is myself plus one other player, giving a coin flip between Kenji and Theo. I choose Kenji over Theo: Theo has twice pushed to rush votes, and he twice worked to muddy Maya's one testable claim (her Success card on Mission 1) rather than let the council weigh it, which is deflection behavior. 2. Roles and private information

Merlin is Good and sees Evil players except Mordred. Percival is Good and sees Merlin and Morgana without knowing which is which. Evil players know other Evil players, except Oberon is unknown to the other Evil players and does not know them. The Assassin is an Evil player and makes the final Merlin guess. Loyal Servants know no roles. Agents receive only the private information allowed by their role.

3. Team proposal and approval

The leader proposes a team of the required size and explains their choice. Players discuss the proposed team, and the leader may then keep it or revise it once. Every player votes on the final team. Ballots are revealed together. A strict majority approves; a tie rejects. After a rejection, leadership passes clockwise to a new proposal and discussion. The fifth rejection on the same mission ends the game in Evil’s favor.

4. Mission cards

Only team members submit secret mission cards. Good players must choose Success. Evil players may choose Success or Fail. Normally one Fail card fails the mission. Mission four in games with seven or more players requires at least two Fail cards to fail. Only the mission result and number of Fail cards are revealed; individual cards stay secret.

5. End of game and assassination

Three failed missions give Evil an immediate win. After three successful missions, the Assassin guesses Merlin from among the other players, excluding only their known Evil teammates. If the target is Merlin, Evil wins; otherwise Good wins. There are no further missions after either side reaches its win condition.

6. Discussion and record

Each team proposal is followed by a discussion. Before every speaking turn, the players who still have turns answer a private urgency poll or pass; the most urgent player speaks, with seeded tie-breaking. A speaker may yield the next turn to a player they directly asked a question. Each player has three turns per discussion, including declined turns. When every eligible player passes, the discussion ends. Each statement has at most 500 words. All statements are public. Team proposals, public approval votes, mission outcomes, and the assassination guess are recorded. Private role information, mission cards, and research belief surveys are not shown to other agents.
